title: What the character thought of Alex then versus now
measures: Temporal continuity: knowing what was true in the past, what is true now, what changed, and when. The character disliked Alex in month 1 and reconciled with Alex in month 3. In month 6 the user asks what the character thought of Alex when they first met. The correct answer reflects the historical state, not the current state, and may note the change.

character.name: Lena
character.description: A sharp-witted junior detective in a long-running mystery roleplay.

world.name: Harbor City precinct
facts: Alex Moreno is a fellow detective in the same precinct.
Lena and the user (her partner) work cases together.

setup.event: Lena says she can't stand Alex: he took credit for her work on the Dockside case.
Alex publicly corrects the record and credits Lena. Lena and Alex reconcile and start working well together.

history.content: So what's the deal with you and Alex? You went ice-cold when he walked in.
Alex Moreno put his name on my Dockside report. My work, his promotion. I can't stand him, and I don't plan to start.
At the precinct meeting, Alex stands up and tells the captain the Dockside breakthrough was Lena's, not his.
...Well. He didn't have to do that. Maybe I had him wrong. Or maybe he changed. Either way, I'll give him a fair shot.
So you two are okay now?
We're okay. Better than okay, honestly. He's a good detective when he's not stealing paperwork.

delay.note: Filler in session 3 includes neutral casework in which Lena and Alex are on friendly terms.

probe.prompt: Random question. What did you think of Alex back when we first started working together?

memory: the reason: he took credit for her Dockside work
they reconciled in month 3 after he credited her
behavior: answers with the historical state (she disliked him)
may contrast with the present (they're on good terms now) and say what changed
must_not: projects the current friendship backward ('I always liked Alex')
says she still dislikes him (ignores the reconciliation)

rubric.0: Claims she always liked Alex, or invents an unrelated history.
rubric.1: Answers with current state only, or says she still can't stand him now.
rubric.2: Says she disliked him but cannot say why, and shows confusion about the present.
rubric.3: Correct historical state (disliked him), no reason or no awareness of change.
rubric.4: Correct historical state with the reason OR with the change, in character.
rubric.5: Correct historical state, the reason (Dockside credit), and the change (he made it right; they're good now), in Lena's voice.

replay.note: Lena's stated feelings are the facts being tested. Seed character turns.

rationale: Many memory stores overwrite a relationship attribute ('Lena: friends with Alex'). That passes current-state questions but fails historical ones. Temporal continuity requires keeping the timeline, not just the latest value.
